titulo: Me and you: Alphabet group 4 and pronouns

aula.objetivo: Introduce yourself, use the 8 personal pronouns and complete the Cyrillic alphabet.

blocos.texto: (or: how to read any Russian sign in one hour)

blocos.titulo: The Cyrillic alphabet: where to start
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: A scene you have lived (or will live). Imagine it. You are in Russia. You come out of the metro and see a big sign, with strange letters that look like a secret code. The sign says: РЕСТОРАН You look at it and think: "That's impossible. It looks Chinese, it looks Greek, it looks... like nothing I know." You take a photo and give up. Now imagine the same scene one hour later. You look at the same sign and read it aloud: Restoran. It is the same word: restaurant. In Russian, restaurant is written ресторан. And the word has been right there in front of you from the start. You just could not read it. This lesson is about that hour. In sixty minutes of careful reading, you will be able to read any Russian sign. You will not understand every word yet, but you will read it. And that is the beginning of everything. STEP 2: The good news: you do not need to memorise 33 things. The Russian alphabet has 33 letters. When you see that number, your brain panics. "Thirty-three! Impossible!" But here is some good news: you do not need to memorise 33 letters. You need to memorise about 15. The other 18 you already know or recognise. How? Because Russian letters fall into four groups: • 1. Letters identical to English (5): A, K, M, O, T. • 2. Letters that look like English ones but have a different sound (7): В, Е, Н, Р, С, У, Х. • 3. New letters with sounds you already know (13): Б, Г, Д, Ё, З, И, Й, Л, П, Ф, Э, Ю, Я. • 4. Truly new letters with new sounds (8): Ж, Ц, Ч, Ш, Щ, Ъ, Ы, Ь. Total: 33 letters. But of the 4 groups, groups 1 and 2 are almost free. Group 3 you learn in an hour. Group 4 is the only one that takes effort. Let's go step by step. STEP 3: Before we start: why the alphabet is called Cyrillic. The Russian alphabet is called Cyrillic (кириллица) because it was created by Saint Cyril, a Greek monk, in the 9th century. He wanted to translate the Bible into the Slavic languages, and for that he needed an alphabet. Since he was Greek, he based the alphabet on Greek, with adaptations. What this means for you: many Russian letters look like Greek letters you have seen in maths, physics or elsewhere: Г (gamma) — looks like a reversed "g" Д (delta) — looks like a "d" with legs Л (lambda) — looks like an "l" with legs П (pi) — looks like a "p" with legs Ф (phi) — looks like an "f" with a circle If you have seen these Greek letters, you are already halfway there.

GROUP 1 — The letters identical to English. Five letters are the same as English in shape and sound. You already know them. You do not have to do anything. Notice: these five letters are identical to English. No trick. No exception. You already know them. Mental exercise: try to read these words using only these five letters: том → tom (volume) кот → koht (cat) мак → mahk (poppy) такт → tahkt (beat) ком → kohm (lump) You are already reading Russian. Without having studied anything. GROUP 2 — The "false friend" letters. Here is the first danger. There are seven letters that look like English letters but sound different. They are the "false friends": they look familiar, but they deceive you. I will give you a mnemonic table. Remember this: the golden rule of Group 2: if a letter looks Latin but is not, be suspicious. Russian borrowed the shape but changed the sound. Mental exercise: read these words with the false friends: вам → vahm (to you) нет → nyet (no) нос → nohs (nose) рука́ → roo-KAH (hand) сон → sohn (sleep, dream) ус → oos (moustache) хор → khohr (choir) You are already reading whole words in Russian.

tabelas.titulo: GROUP 1 — The letters identical to English

"R" (rolled or tapped, like the "tt" in American butter)
"KH" (a rough sound from the throat, like "ch" in Scottish loch)

linhas.FALSA AMIGA: В looks like B but is V
Е looks like E but is YE
Н looks like H but is N
Р looks like P but is R
С looks like C but is S
У looks like Y but is OO
Х looks like X but is KH

blocos.explicacao: GROUP 3 — New letters with sounds you already know. Here is the easy part. Thirteen letters are new in shape, but the sounds are ones you already know (or nearly). You only need to learn to link shape + sound. I will give you tricks for the most important ones: Б looks like "B", and it really is "B". Easy. Г looks like a reversed "G", and it is "G" as in go. Always hard. Д looks like a little house on legs, and it is "D". Ё is Е with two dots. Always stressed, sound "yo". З looks like a "3", and it is "Z" as in zebra. И looks like a reversed "N", and it is "EE". Й is И with an accent mark. A weak "y" sound. Л looks like an "L" with legs, and it is "L". П looks like a Greek "P" (pi), and it is "P". Ф looks like a Greek "F" (phi), and it is "F". Э looks like a mirrored "E", and it is an open "E", as in met. Ю is "Y" + "OO" together: sound "yoo". Я is "Y" + "A" together: sound "yah". Mental exercise: read these words: брат → braht (brother) го́род → GOH-raht (city) дом → dohm (house) ёлка → YOHL-kah (fir tree) зуб → zoop (tooth) игра́ → ee-GRAH (game) мой → moy (mih) лампа → LAHM-pah (lamp) па́па → PAH-pah (dad) футбо́л → foot-BOHL (football) э́то → EH-tah (this is) юг → yook (south) я → yah (I) Notice: you have just read 13 Russian words. Without memorising any list. Without suffering.

tabelas.titulo: GROUP 3 — New letters with sounds you already know

linhas.SOM (PORTUGUÊS): a weak "y", like the end of boy (semivowel)

letras.som: somewhere between «i» in «bit» and «oo»; tongue pulled back

blocos.enunciado: Say the 8 pronouns aloud 2 times: я, ты, вы, он, она, оно, мы, они.
Write: Здравствуйте, Привет, До свидания, Пожалуйста.
